Provide preliminary pricing for Dedicated pool + ingress burst
action_items: Carlos Rivera: Share LangChain + LlamaIndex sample repo and small benchmark script by 2027-06-25
Maya Patel: Email security docs and draft pricing for 3-month pilot by 2027-06-24
Noah Kim: Confirm internal stakeholders and data residency constraints by 2027-06-30
meeting_header: Date: 2027-06-23 | Time: 15:00-15:48 UTC | Duration: 48 mins | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Noah Kim (CTO - Meridian), Aisha Rahman (Platform Eng), Derek Lo (SRE)
summary: Exploratory discovery to understand Meridian's constraints for onramp to Redwood: deciding between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; integration via SDKs and LangChain/LlamaIndex; gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer wants pilot with predictable throughput and audit logs; has strict KMS/HSM requirement for keys used in embeddings. Action: SE to send sample connectors and run a short benchmark; AE to send security docs and pricing.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Observability and telemetry hooks (OpenTelemetry, traces, token-level cost)
transcript: [00:00] Maya (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros? We have Maya and Carlos from Redwood - Maya is AE, Carlos lead SE. Could you share roles at Meridian?

[00:18] Noah (CTO): Hey, I'm Noah - CTO. Aisha is platform, Derek does SRE. We're evaluating options to run inference for our clinical summaries and search embeddings. Latency matters but cost is also big, so we want to see Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs.

[00:35] Maya: Great, that'll help. Briefly, Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private VPC or on-prem. Carlos will cover integration patterns - SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy options.
[00:48] Carlos (SE): Hi all. Before we deep dive, quick qual: what's your expected QPS and typical sequence lengths? Also do you need data to stay in your VPC?

[01:04] Aisha: Good question. For search and summarization, avg prompt length ~200 tokens, peaks to 1.5k. Baseline is 15 QPS with occasional spikes to 80 QPS for short bursts. Data needs to stay in our VPC for PHI — so Private or a VPC-hosted option is preferred. We also have HSM-backed keys for encryption.
[01:30] Derek: And we need audit logs and per-request tracing, plus role-based access — SSO/SAML. SOC2 compliance is table stakes.

[01:44] Maya: Understood. Private deployment supports customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM integrations. Dedicated can be in our cloud with private networking; Hosted has some VPC peering options but you'd need to check the data residency flow. We'll send SOC2 and KMS notes.
[02:02] Noah: Okay. For integration, our app uses LangChain and some bespoke orchestration. We also have a LlamaIndex-based vector store. How smooth is integration?

[02:15] Carlos: We have SDKs in Python/Node, plus examples for LangChain agents and LlamaIndex connectors. For LlamaIndex, the vectorstore adapter needs just a small shim; we've seen customers swap the API key for a Redwood client and it works. We'll share a sample repo. Note: some customers use the Redwood gateway sidecar pattern to centralize retries and rate limiting.
[02:45] Aisha: That sidecar idea — can it live in our cluster? We prefer not to run SDKs directly from many microservices.

[02:54] Carlos: Yes, sidecar or gateway. Two main patterns: 1) SDK direct calls inside app, 2) centralized gateway/proxy that handles batching, caching, auth, and quotas. Gateway gives you single place for observability and consistent retries. Sidecar scales with pods but can be heavier operationally.
[03:18] Derek: For quotas and rate limits: we need per-tenant and per-route quotas. Bursting up to 4x baseline is okay but should be throttled gracefully. Any built-in quota enforcement?

[03:33] Maya: Redwood has per-token and route quotas, and per-api-key limits. For Dedicated you can configure reserved throughput and burst policies. Gateway/proxy can enforce tenant-level quotas before hitting the runtime. We'll demonstrate policy configs in the pilot.
[03:50] Noah: Observability — we use OpenTelemetry and DataDog. We want token-level cost attribution, latency percentiles, traces, and KV cache hit rates. Can Redwood emit open spans and telemetry?

[04:05] Carlos: Yes, we support exporting traces via OTLP, plus webhook traces into DataDog. The Console exposes token-level breakdown and per-model tracing. Small caveat: some internal metric names might differ; we can map them. Also there's a sampling option for high-QPS routes to control telemetry volume.
[04:32] Aisha: You mentioned caching — prefix caching or KV cache — how transparent is that to the app? Could it change semantics?

[04:42] Carlos: Automatic prefix/KV caching is opt-in per-route. It preserves response consistency for deterministic prompts, but for non-deterministic sampling you'll want to disable. We'll review your prompt patterns in the pilot. There's also a cache invalidation TTL you can set.
[05:01] Noah: On models, do you support both open models and Redwood-verified variants? We plan to evaluate smaller quantized models to cut cost.

[05:11] Maya: Yes. Hosted includes curated models, Dedicated and Private can host compatible variants. We also provide recommendations for quantization and kernel selection per workload. Our Optimize toolkit gives batch/caching suggestions.
[05:26] Derek: Is model fallback supported? If a Dedicated node is full can calls route to Hosted? We need graceful degradation.
[05:35] Carlos: Yes, smart routing policies allow fallback to compatible model variants or other regions — configurable per-route. For strict offline/on-prem needs you can disable fallback.
[05:46] Aisha: Security — HSM: we manage customer keys via KMS/HSM. How does Redwood integrate?

[05:57] Maya: For Private we support customer-managed KMS and HSMs. For Dedicated we can set up a KMS integration (cloud KMS or HSM appliances). We'll include specifics in the security pack. Also SSO, RBAC, and audit logs are all available for Enterprise plans.

[06:14] Noah: Great. Practical question: we use LangChain chains with multiple LLM calls per user request; we'd like routing decisions to be policy-driven — e.g., cheap model for embeddings, higher-quality for final summarization. Can Redwood support per-call model selection?

[06:31] Carlos: Absolutely — you can route by route name, header, or cost threshold. The gateway can rewrite requests to route to different model variants and keep the rest of the app unchanged. Many teams use the gateway to inject a 'routing hint' header.
[06:47] Maya: Maybe a quick demo in the pilot: LangChain example showing embeddings on a quantized model and summarization on a larger model in one workflow.
[06:55] Aisha: That would be ideal. Also, what about token accounting across a chain of calls? We need aggregated cost per user action for billing and audit.

[07:06] Carlos: The Console can aggregate per-transaction when you provide a transaction-id header. We also export per-token logs to your S3/URI if you want offline cost recon. There's a small ingestion fee for long-term retention.
[07:22] Noah: On performance — for our 80 QPS spikes we need sub-200ms tail latency on short prompts. What SLAs can you provide?

[07:34] Maya: SLA varies by product. Dedicated has SLA-backed latency and uptime guarantees; Hosted has best-effort but predictable performance for common configs. We'll propose Dedicated for predictable 99th pct latency. Carlos can walk benchmark results from similar customers.

[07:50] Carlos: We have a benchmark sheet we can share. For short prompts we've sustained 120ms p50 and 220ms p99 in a similar setup with batching and KV caching disabled for low latency. I'll attach the sheet.

[08:06] Aisha: About the gateway/proxy — we prefer the gateway approach to centralize telemetry and quotas. What deployment options exist? A single managed gateway in Redwood vs running their gateway in customer VPC?

[08:20] Carlos: Both. Managed gateway is easiest (Hosted) but requires some network peering. You can also deploy our gateway as a sidecar or a central ingress appliance in your VPC. For PHI, customers often run the gateway on-prem or in their VPC so requests never leave their network — then we only provide control plane access.
[08:41] Derek: If we run gateway in our VPC, can we still use Redwood Console for traces and rollouts?

[08:48] Maya: Yes, the control plane can be hybrid: telemetry and rollouts are reported to the Console while preserving PII in your VPC. We can limit what telemetry leaves your network and provide filtered metrics. We'll document telemetry fields and PII redaction options.
[09:05] Noah: Licensing and pricing — how do pilots work? We'd like a 6-8 week pilot with a Dedicated pool and ability to test burst policies. Any minimum commitment?

[09:17] Maya: Pilots are flexible. For Dedicated we typically ask for a 3-month reserved capacity for predictability, but we can do a scoped pilot for 6-8 weeks with capped usage. We'll send a pricing sketch for a small Dedicated pool plus ingress burst credits.
[09:34] Aisha: On the SDKs, does Redwood provide a LangChain Agent integration or do we need to write adapters?

[09:41] Carlos: We provide code samples: a LangChain LLM wrapper, an embeddings client for vectorstores, and a LlamaIndex connector. Most customers copy/paste the wrapper and replace the key. For more complex chains we recommend using the gateway to centralize logic.
[09:57] Derek: Some words get mis-typed by our infra — like KV cache being called 'K V cash' in earlier docs — just flagging we'll want the exact implementation details.
[10:05] Carlos: Haha, noted. We'll make sure to include accurate docs and a short runbook for cache semantics.
[10:12] Maya: Quick pivot — a security question from procurement: can we support audit logs going to their SIEM?
[10:20] Noah: Yes, we need to push logs to Splunk and also have tamper-evident audit trails.
[10:26] Maya: We support log forwarding to Splunk/S3 and have append-only audit logs in Private deployments. We'll include SIEM integration steps.
[10:35] Aisha: Can you talk about data retention and deletion? For compliance we need data purged after 30 days unless flagged for review.

[10:43] Carlos: Retention windows are configurable per-tenant. For Hosted we retain minimal request metadata by default but can set custom retention and deletion via API. For Private, it's under your control.
[10:56] Noah: One more technical: we have an in-house optimizer that does batching across requests — will Redwood's batching add on top of ours and cause unexpected delays?

[11:07] Carlos: Redwood does continuous batching in the runtime; if you already batch upstream, you can set the runtime to bypass additional batching. We have parameters for max-latency windows and batch size to tune for low-latency workloads.
[11:24] Derek: On quotas again — we need per-team, per-route, and per-user quotas, with alerting when thresholds are near. Does Redwood support webhooks for quota breach alerts?
[11:36] Maya: Yes, quota alerts via webhook, email, and Console dashboards. You can configure soft and hard limits and set pre-threshold alarms.
[11:48] Aisha: For the pilot, what do you need from us to get started?

[11:54] Carlos: Ideally: a small sample prompt set, a TM for expected QPS profile, an example LangChain chain you want to run, and confirmation on network pattern (peered vs in-VPC gateway). We'll run a micro-benchmark and demo the LangChain example.
[12:08] Noah: We'll prepare sample payloads and a dev VPC for the gateway. Also we'll need the LangChain sample earlier you mentioned.

[12:16] Maya: Action recap: Carlos will share the LangChain/LlamaIndex repo and benchmark sheet; Maya sends security docs and pricing; Noah confirms stakeholders and VPC details. Schedule pilot kickoff for week of July 6th. Any blockers?
[12:32] Derek: Only internal legal sign-off; procurement may ask for SOC2 and encryption details but should be standard.
[12:38] Maya: We'll add that to the packet. Any other product questions?
[12:42] Aisha: One thing — metrics naming. We use strict tags (team, env, tenant) in OTEL. Will Redwood mapping support custom attributes?
[12:52] Carlos: Yes, you can map your OTEL attributes to Redwood Console fields. We'll include mapping examples in the integration checklist.
[13:02] Noah: Regarding LlamaIndex vectorstore, we store vectors in our managed store. Do we need to rehydrate embeddings in Redwood?

[13:10] Carlos: You can either call embeddings from Redwood and store vectors back in your store, or send precomputed embeddings. For latency-sensitive retrieval, many customers compute locally and only call the LLM for ranking/augmentation.
[13:25] Aisha: Pricing clarity: how granular is per-token billing, and can we get a forecast for cost if we run at average 15 QPS?

[13:36] Maya: Billing is per-token for generation and per-embedding unit for embeddings. We'll run a cost projection in the pricing doc; include your prompt distribution and QPS and we'll model quantized vs full models.
[13:50] Derek: Any experimental features we should be aware of? Like automatic re-try logic that could double-charge?
[13:58] Carlos: Retries are idempotent-aware if you pass an idempotency key. Console will attribute retries separately unless it's deduped by the runtime; we'll explain best practices.
[14:10] Aisha: For audit, we want a binary proof of who called what model when — is that available?
[14:18] Maya: We have append-only request logs with identity and model version. For Private you can host the logs and we can provide a signed manifest if needed.
[14:28] Noah: Any red flags from your side on our architecture?
[14:31] Carlos: Nothing major. Main area: ensure gateway in-VPC has low-latency path to your vectorstore. Also validate HSM connectivity for KMS early in the pilot.

[14:44] Noah: Good to know. Let's talk pilot specifics now: timeline and success criteria. Our success metrics: p99 <300ms for short prompts, cost per user action under X, and secure handling of PHI (auditable).
[14:58] Maya: We'll propose pilot success criteria aligned with that: p99 target, cost modeling, integration completeness (LangChain + LlamaIndex working), and security checklist completion.
[15:08] Aisha: Sounds good. Any dependencies on their side? We'll need RBAC mappings and sample transaction-id header to test aggregated billing.
[15:18] Carlos: We'll provide a small integration test harness that emits transaction-id and demonstrates aggregator in Console. We'll run a short load test to validate quotas and burst behavior.
[15:28] Derek: One last thing — we integrate with an API gateway (Kong). Will that sit in front of Redwood gateway or will Redwood gateway sit behind Kong?
[15:36] Carlos: Either. Common pattern: Kong in edge, Redwood gateway behind for LLM-specific routing and observability. We'll include an example deployment diagram.
[15:47] Maya: Great. Recap of next steps and I'll follow up via email. Thanks everyone, we'll send docs and schedule the kickoff.
[15:56] Noah: Thanks all. Bye.
[16:00] (call ends)
